steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease an 8-inch square baking dish.
Fry bacon in a skillet over medium-high heat until nearly crisp, about 5 minutes. Add honey and stir until the foaming subsides. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon to a plate to cool.
Mix brown sugar, melted butter, white sugar, and vanilla in a large bowl; mix in eggs.
Sift flour, cocoa powder, and salt together in a bowl; add to the egg mixture. Fold bacon and chocolate chips into the mixture; pour into the prepared baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, 25 to 35 minutes. Allow brownies to cool for 20 minutes before cutting into squares.

raw_recipe.headline: Bacon Brownies
raw_recipe.description: Enjoy this unforgettable recipe for bacon brownies. The combo of salty bacon with rich chocolate is surprisingly delicious. You'll be back for more.
raw_recipe.name: Bacon Brownies

review.reviewBody: I really liked these. I added most of the bacon inside and left a few for the top to decorate the plate. Really rich. Tasted great warm.. hope they taste good tomorrow as well

I made this and added the chocolate ganache on he top from the fudgey bacon supreme recipe. My first batch of bacon I cooked too long before adding the honey, so I put it to the side and gave it to my bacon loving neice because it was perfect for snacking. The second round of bacon came out better. I loved the brownie and will use the recipe for just that as I have nevertheless been a good brownie maker, even boxed ones came out horrible for me. I am not certain how these really tasted because everyone was so full from Christmas Eve diver, they didn't taste it while I was there. I admit to being disappointed because I thought they tasted pretty good, although next time I think I will just put bacon on the top instead of on the inside too. The brownies are really chocolatey and rich and sometimes the bacon on the inside seemed too salty. A small piece of this goes along way. I am glad I added the ganache topping though. I baked the brownie, cooled it in the fridge, put the ganache on top, then placed bacon so that it defined where each piece would be. So he bacon on top was not cooked beyond what had been done in the pan with the honey. I like bacon less crispy, so it was fine for me. I also agree with a few of the other reviews that said people kind of turn their nose up when you say what it is, so be prepared. I was really proud of how this came out, but if I make it again, I will take it for something other than dinner so people are more inclined to taste it (and to people

I'm giving this recipe a 5 star rating because the construction crew that I made it for LOVED these brownies. I've only realized now that I read the recipe wrong. I wondered why it said 1 and a 1/4 pound of bacon! Such an odd amount. oh boy! I need new reading glasses. I cooked the bacon in the oven and then crumbled it because it was easier for me. No wonder! But the excessive amount of bacon worked (I reserved some to place on top before baking) Thank you for the great recipe!

This recipe is AMAZING. It's the perfect chewy moist brownie, and the bacon is subtle. I didn't put the honey on the bacon when frying it, but they turned out fine. I used bacon to garnish the top, along with a peanut butter/chocolate frosting to enhance the salty sweet combination. I'm definitely keeping this just for the brownie recipe alone. Yum!!

MAKE THE BACON EXTRA CRISPY!! These brownies are rich and moist, and the bacon adds an excellent crispy, salty surprise! I can see why other reviewers may have had issues with the bacon if they didn't cook it well enough. Personally, I BAKED maple flavored bacon until very crispy and then crumbled it for the recipe. I didn't bother with the honey. When the bacon pieces are small and crunchy they are the perfect addition to the brownies. Don't forget to save some bacon pieces to sprinkle on top for visual effect.

This was interesting. VERY RICH... and I like the combination. I made the bacon in the microwave I put Four prices, in for four minutes. And the bacon came out perfectly fine. I skipped the honey as well but made additional bacon and mixed the honey, and some brown sugar. I will make this again personally I think people would be too skeptical to try it but I love it. Thanks for sharing your recipe!

These are really good, my whole family loves them and so do my friends at school. One thing I recommend tho is putting chocolate chips at the bottom of the pan before you pour in the batter, and as they cook put powder sugar on top. It makes then bout twice and good. They melt in your mouth.
Pretty darn good! Made as called for with bacon. My husband loves them. My mom likes the brownie mix with chocolate chips and pecans- no bacon.
PMS emergency ! Very Chocolately with the saltiness of bacon perfection. Suggest cooking bacon til its crunchy or you will be chewing alot.

absolutely amazing! I substituted 1/2 the butter with bacon fat, and skipped the honey, 
Mmmmm!

Agree great brownie recipe. I made some for at home and was a big hit! I made a double batch and took them to work. Had some questions, like bacon and brownies?? They tried them and cleaned out the container. I added two things to the bacon, 2 TBS agave nectar and 1 TBS brown sugar. Very good!
These worked out awesome! Some of my guests were hesitant to try brownies with bacon, but as soon as they tried them, they were pretty easily won over. I'd definitely make these again.
Followed the recipe and turned out great! Just had to bake a little longer!
I wouldn’t cook the bacon to quite so done and I would make the pieces a bit bigger . But I thought they were very tasty and will make them again and again!

I baked these the minimum amount of time, because I had other things needing to bake after, and it definitely needed the longer time. Had to eat them with a spoon, even after they had time to cool and set. Still tasted pretty good, so will probably make them again, just will bake them longer.
I love the brownie mix...With Out the bacon. Five stars for the brownie mix, I just didn't find the bacon good at all. Just my preference.
These turned out great, the pan was cleaned before I could blink and several people asked for the recipe. I did add a touch of caramel drizzle on top too.
Nice chewy brownie with the extra taste of sweetened bacon when eaten warm from the oven ---- but next day when cool the taste of bacon is gone and brownie a little drier.
I "accidentally" used a whole pound of bacon. Oops! This was delicious!!!!
Excellent brownies! I didn't add honey to the bacon because I didn't have any, but the brownies were so good, it didn't matter. Thanks for the recipe.
